Every post is a folder in `posts/` holding an `index.qmd` file, together with
anything the post uses: data, images, a bibliography. The folder name starts
with the date, such that the posts sort in the file browser as they do on the
blog. A new post is started by making a folder such as
`posts/2026-11-20-phonon-results/`, adding an `index.qmd` file to it, and
copying in the front matter shown below.

## The front matter

The block between the `---` lines at the top of the file is the *front
matter*. It is written in YAML and holds everything about the post that is not
its text. The front matter of this post is

```yaml
---
title: "Writing a post"
description: "How a post is put together, ..."
author: "Tolborg Group"
date: 2026-11-01
categories: [guide, markdown]
bibliography: references.bib
---
```

The title, description, date and categories appear in the list of posts on the
front page, where the categories also work as filters. Adding `draft: true`
keeps a post off the published blog while it is being written; drafts are
still shown by `pixi run preview`.

## Markdown

The text itself is Markdown, so **bold**, *italics*, `code`,
[links](https://quarto.org) and lists work as usual:

- Lists are written with `-`,
- numbered lists with `1.`,
- and nesting with an indent.

Code blocks are fenced with three backticks and the name of the language, which
gives syntax highlighting:

```python
def lennard_jones(r, epsilon=1.0, sigma=1.0):
    return 4 * epsilon * ((sigma / r) ** 12 - (sigma / r) ** 6)
```

Code blocks like this one are only displayed. Code that is *run* when the post
is rendered is written with braces, ```` ```{python} ````, which is the topic of
[the next post](../2026-11-05-python-figures/index.qmd).

## Equations

Equations are written in LaTeX, inline between single dollar signs, such as
$E = mc^2$, or displayed between double dollar signs. A label after the closing
dollars makes the equation numbered and referable:

$$
V(r) = 4\varepsilon \left[ \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{12}
       - \left(\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)^{6} \right]
$$ {#eq-lj}

@eq-lj is the Lennard-Jones potential. The same `@` syntax refers to figures
(`@fig-…`), tables (`@tbl-…`) and sections (`@sec-…`).

## Citations

With a BibTeX file named in the front matter, `[@kohn1965]` cites an entry
[@kohn1965], `@hohenberg1964` cites it in the text, as in
@hohenberg1964, and the reference list is added at the end of the post. The
BibTeX entries are the same as for LaTeX, so they can be copied from a paper's
`references.bib`.

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
Callouts draw attention to a remark. There are five kinds: `note`, `tip`,
`important`, `warning` and `caution`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## A collapsed callout with a title

Its content is only shown when the title is clicked. Useful for details that
most readers will skip.
:::

## Tabs and margin notes

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Pixi

```bash
pixi add numpy
```

## pip

```bash
pip install numpy
```
:::

Short remarks can go in the margin instead of the
text.[This is a margin note, written as `[...]{.aside}` or with a `.column-margin` div.]{.aside}
Footnotes work too.^[And are collected at the end of the post.]

## Images

An image in the post folder is included with

```markdown
![A caption](figure.png){#fig-name width=70%}
```

where the label and width are optional. Figures made by Python code in the
post do not need this, as shown in the next post.
